title: Flagged for Review
intro: Every item below is something the verification pass could not confirm from an official source, or a value that was left blank rather than filled in. None of these blocks the site: they are published here so they can be reviewed and assigned. Each item carries the official link it relates to. Items F13 to F25 were added on 2026-11-14 by the horizon build and the refresh session, and concern the fresh three-day horizon, the refresh path, and what could not be refreshed. Items F26 to F37 were added on 2026-11-14 (UTC) by the official-source check (COORDINATION.md §23): conflicts between builds, sign conventions, counts, stale finals, and the 11/17 capture gap. Items F38 to F39 were added on 2026-11-14 by the final integration session (COORDINATION.md section 21): a leaderboard tier-label defect (found and fixed in engine/leaderboard.py) and one injury-row attribution resolved against the official roster page. F13 and F14 were resolved the same morning by the integration refresh; F15, F16 and F19 were updated to the 04:15 AM ET injury edition. Items F40 to F46 were added on 2026-11-14 (UTC) by the measured prop-variance build (COORDINATION.md section 26): what could not be captured, the staleness and its reconciliation, why the parlay rho stays an assumption, the half-filed game-day report, the limits of a 3-4 game window, the F31 resolution, and the rows that carry a dash instead of a link.

items.title: NBA.com standings table is not machine-readable
items.detail: The official standings page renders its table client-side; a plain fetch returns only the tie-break procedure text, not the table. Won-lost records were therefore taken from the official Stats > Teams Advanced table and from each game's own NBA.com game page instead. Every record on this site has one of those two links.
items.affected: Team records on the Lines and Picks pages
items.suggested_action: Add a headless-browser capture to the refresh job if the standings table itself is ever needed; today it is not.

items.title: Player minutes are only known for 50 of 465 players
items.detail: The official Players Traditional table publishes 465 rows across 10 pages; only page 1 (the 50 highest scorers) is present in the page source available to a plain fetch. Minutes for the other 415 players were left blank, not estimated. Two consequences: (a) the availability impact on the Injuries page is a measured LOWER BOUND and is 0.00 for several teams whose injured players fall outside the top 50; (b) player-prop coverage is limited to those 50 players.
items.affected: Injuries page impact column; Picks page player props (S7, S8)
items.suggested_action: Backfill per-team minutes from the same official table filtered by team, or from official box scores. Until then, treat the impact column as a floor and read the minutes-coverage column next to it.

items.title: No official-book price exists, so 'the line we bet against' is a model, not a market
items.detail: No sportsbook price is published by an NBA-operated source, so no official link can be attached to one. The site therefore bets the originated line against a deliberately naive REFERENCE line built from the same official ratings. A 'win' here means the model beat the naive model, not that it beat a book. Real expected value cannot be stated untilmarket prices are logged.
items.affected: Every strategy result, the leaderboard, and the word 'edge' throughout
items.suggested_action: Log closing prices from a licensed odds source into data/raw/market.json with a per-row source field. Until then, read 'units' as model-vs-naive-model units.

items.title: Five modelling constants are choices, not official measurements
items.detail: Shrinkage constant k, the offense/defence split of an availability loss (alpha = 0.60), the availability impact coefficient (15.0 net-rating points per 100 possessions at 100% minutes lost), the status weights (Out 1.00 / Doubtful 0.70 / Questionable 0.35 / Probable 0.10), and the three player-prop multipliers are all modelling choices. k is now derived by an empirical-Bayes reliability calculation, but the single-game noise term in that calculation is estimated on the test window, so k is partly test-informed. A fixed-k sensitivity sweep is published on the Validation page.
items.affected: Model page; every originated number
items.suggested_action: Re-estimate all five on a full season of game logs once the backfill exists; until then they are published with their derivation, not hidden.

items.title: No archived injury reports, so the availability strategy is ungraded
items.detail: Only the 2026-11-13 05:15 PM edition of the official injury report was captured. Strategy S6 (availability shock) and gate G7 (flip every Questionable player to Out) therefore have no graded record. They are shown as UNGRADED / NOT RUN rather than being scored with substituted data.
items.affected: S6, gate G7
items.suggested_action: The refresh job should archive every edition it sees; grading can then start once ~30 graded S6 plays exist.

items.title: Parlay and same-game-parlay correlations are model-derived, not measured
items.detail: Measuring the correlation between two legs needs play-by-play, which was not captured. The rho values used to price S9 and S10 are derived from the structure of the model, not from data. The side/total value of 0.00 is a mathematical property of the additive model under equal team-score variances; the player-market values are estimates.
items.affected: Correlations page; S9 and S10 pricing
items.suggested_action: Estimate empirical correlations from a season of play-by-play or from official box scores; they are labelled MODEL-DERIVED everywhere until then.

items.title: Refresh path executed - and what it proved
items.detail: Executed on 2026-11-14 by session arena/d6918959-nba1 via seven workflow runs (43540726330, 43541446595, 43541959088, 43542957208, 43543433956, 43543718982, 43544324610) on GitHub's runners, after the fetch client was given the web-client header set the reachability probe proved returns HTTP 200. Results: (1) the finals capture now parses the pages' embedded JSON and re-verified all 51 committed finals for 2026-11-06..11-12 against the official pages with 0 mismatches; (2) injury-report editions are discovered and archived with SHA-256, and the 2026-11-14 editions correctly record as unavailable at capture time; (3) scheduled runs no longer push to main - they open a pull request (cross-session request R7 / audit item I-01); (4) the team-advanced and schedule captures are still blocked - see F13 and F14. Captures never overwrite a committed snapshot; promotion stays a separate verified step.

items.title: Every strategy is still short of the 30-play sample gate
items.detail: The out-of-sample window is now 51 games (2026-11-06 to 2026-11-12), all of them predicted from ratings computed on 2026-10-20 to 2026-11-05. The best-graded strategy, S1, has 23 graded plays at 16-7 (+7.55 model units, 32.8% ROI at -110). Its exact binomial p-value is 0.093 and the Wilson 95% interval on its hit rate is [0.491, 0.844] - the lower bound sits below the 0.5238 break-even, so the skill gate fails. Every other strategy has fewer graded plays. The residual standard deviation of the game margin is 17.4 points, so a swing of three or four games is well inside chance.
items.affected: Every gate result on the Validation page
items.suggested_action: Treat every result as provisional. The window cannot grow further without backfilling 2026-10-20 to 2026-11-05 results - which would then have to be split into a new training period and test period.

items.title: Back-to-back detection is complete from 2026-11-07 onward
items.detail: Rest flags are computed from the captured results, which now begin 2026-11-06. Back-to-backs running into 2026-11-07 and later are therefore fully detected (12 home, 9 away across the window). Back-to-backs running into 2026-11-06 itself are still not detected, because no game before 2026-11-06 was captured. The bias this leaves is toward zero, so the fitted penalty of 6.10 points is if anything understated.

items.title: Two projection sets disagree on the same games
items.detail: The landing-page lines (site/data/lines.json, Build B) and the horizon lines (data/derived/horizon_lines.json, Build D) project different home margins for the same games. On the 17 games that carry a Build B point-spread pick, the two margins differ by 0.8 to 11.8 points (all 17 differ by more than 0.5), and 2 of the 17 name opposite favourites (DAL@CLE, PHI@BKN). Build B's ratings training window is 10/20-11/05/2026 per site/data/meta.json; Build D uses team ratings through games of 11/12. The site does not say which set feeds the horizon. Checked 2026-11-14 UTC by scripts/source_check.py (Source Check, section 5).

items.title: 'Spread (home)' fields hold the home margin, with the opposite sign to a book spread
items.detail: In Build B (site/data/lines.json: ref_spread_home, model_spread_home) and Build D (line_spread_home) the stored value is the home team's projected margin: a negative value means the home team is projected to lose. Build A's originated_spread_home uses the conventional sign. Example: DEN@NOP, model_spread_home -9.6, is the projected home margin, so DEN (away) is projected to win by 9.6. Test: the S1 side agrees with the home-margin reading in 16 of 16 Build B rows and with the conventional reading in 0 of 16. The same site therefore shows two sign conventions under similar labels.

items.suggested_action: One roster-page read per team (nets, mavs, bulls) supplies the ids; scripts/prop_variance.py then prices them with no further code. Reviewer: approve or defer.

items.title: Every prop baseline on the horizon is one to two games stale and the page does not say so
items.detail: The season averages behind the props were transcribed on 2026-11-13 from the official Per Game table. Recomputing each of the ten captured players (baseline x games played, plus the games since) reproduces what NBA.com prints now for 10 of 10, inside the rounding of a one-decimal average - so the figures are correct for the date they were taken and simply not current. Ty Jerome 26.2 -> 25.4 and Giannis 27.7 -> 28.5 are the largest moves; nothing was wrong and nothing has been refreshed.
items.affected: Player Props page; any prop comparison made after 2026-11-13
items.suggested_action: Print an as-of date on the props table and re-pull the season table on the morning of each slate. The reconciliation itself is now a check the builder can run: any player whose recomputed average misses the live page is a transcription error, not staleness.

items.title: The same-game-parlay rho is still an assumption - a Last-5 window cannot measure it
items.detail: Seven pairs of captured players share at least one game. The best pair (Murray and Jokic) shares three, and reads rho 0.82 on points; pairs with one or two shared games cannot be read at all. Nothing about the pricing on the Correlations page changes as a result: it keeps its declared rho, and this is the measured evidence for why it must stay labelled an assumption. A usable estimate needs 30-50 shared games per pair, i.e. a season-long game-log capture for the players whose props get parlayed - not a Last-5 block.
items.affected: Correlations page; every same-game parlay price on the Picks page
items.suggested_action: Reviewer: choose between (a) a season game-log capture for a small named set of parlay-eligible players, (b) keeping the declared rho and labelling every parlay price with it, or (c) suspending prop legs inside parlays until (a) exists. SG17 writes it up.

items.title: Today's lines and props are priced against a half-filed injury report
items.detail: The newest official edition at 10:30 UTC (11/14 04:30 AM ET) carries 26 named designations for the day, but five of the ten teams had NOT YET SUBMITTED: New Orleans, Cleveland, Memphis, Chicago and Miami. The league rule requires a game-day report between 11:00 and 13:00 local, which had not opened when this was read. The site's injury page and the horizon lines were cut against the 11/13 05:15 PM ET edition; comparing the two editions finds zero rows new or changed, so nothing stale was found - but nothing game-day was confirmable either.
items.affected: Lines and Picks for 2026-11-14; Props for the same date; Injuries page confidence column
items.suggested_action: Re-read the edition inside the 11:00-13:00 window before the first tip and re-run the delta; the refresh workflow already has the URL pattern.

items.title: Limits of the first measured prop variance - read before using any number on that page
items.detail: Three of the site's own making, published rather than smoothed over. (1) The window is 3-4 games per player: the standard deviation itself carries an uncertainty of about SD/sqrt(2(n-1)), i.e. roughly a quarter to a half of the SD, which is why the page prints it per row. (2) Per-player SDs are shrunk toward a cohort figure with k=4 - a modelling choice declared in the script, not an official quantity. (3) The anchor test is contaminated in the season average's favour, and unequal in information (11 games vs 3), so it licenses 'do not chase form' and nothing stronger.
items.affected: Prop Variance page; any sizing decision taken from it
items.suggested_action: Accept as stated, or extend the capture. No figure on the page should be read as statistically significant at this sample size.

items.title: F31 resolved: the 11/14 noon injury edition was unpublished, not missing

The AccessDenied response the earlier session got on the 12:00 PM ET URL is the response for a file the league has not written yet - which is exactly the ambiguity F31 recorded. This closes it: the fetch path works, the timing does not.

items.title: The injury page's "newest edition" label is now more than 12 hours stale
items.detail: data/derived/injury_impact.json and the Injuries page are built from the 11/13 07:30 PM ET edition (and the prop page from the 11/14 04:30 AM ET edition). The official index now carries the 11/14 game-day series from 12:00 AM ET through 01:30 PM ET. Re-read at 2026-11-14T18:50Z, the 01:30 PM ET edition shows four of the five 11/14 teams that had NOT YET SUBMITTED at 04:15 AM ET had filed by the afternoon (New Orleans, Cleveland, Chicago, Miami); only Memphis had not. This session captured the 01:30 PM ET edition into data/live/s14x/ and publishes it beside the older one; it did NOT regenerate the older pages' data, which would move every line.

items.title: Two blocks of the 01:30 PM ET injury PDF lose their team column at a page break
items.detail: The PDF is multi-page and the text reader drops the leading columns on pages 2-5. Two blocks are affected: (1) seven Cleveland Cavaliers rows on page 2 print no team cell but sit inside the DAL@CLE block opened on page 1; (2) six Chicago Bulls rows on page 3 print no team cell. The six were attributed to Chicago on independent official evidence - every one of Claxton, Powell, Sellers, Smith, Swain and Wilson appears on the official Bulls roster (https://www.nba.com/bulls/roster) and none appears on the Nets roster - and the block sits inside CHI@MIN between the Nets block and the Timberwolves block. No name was guessed: a player whose team could not be established from an official page would have been left blank and flagged.

items.title: The official game log is exactly 23 games short of the official standings, uniformly across all 30 teams
items.detail: Recomputing every team's record from data/official/gamelog.json (160 scored games, 2026-10-20..2026-11-13 after this session's 11/13 read) and comparing with the official standings page read at 18:50Z: total points for and against balance exactly (36,240 = 36,240) and wins sum to 160, so the log is internally consistent, but it holds 320 team-games against the standings' 366. The 46 team-games are 23 games. 14 teams are short exactly 1 game, 16 exactly 2, and NO team is short 0 or 3 or more. The 23 missing wins and 23 missing losses balance. The official day pages for 2026-10-24 and 2026-11-02 print no result rows (existing flag F1), so the missing fixtures cannot be named from an official source and are deliberately not named or scored.
items.affected: data/official/gamelog.json; every rest, luck and full-season figure that reads it
items.suggested_action: Capture the two missing dates' results from an official source once they are readable, then rebuild. The gap is uniform, so team-to-team comparisons in data/live/s14x/luck_skill.json survive it; calendar-complete rest figures do not, and are labelled as lower bounds.

items.title: The published props table prices 0 of its 88 rows, while the measured prop-variance study priced 10
items.detail: site/data/props.json carries probability: null on all 88 rows, because the props page was built before the measured-dispersion study landed. data/derived/prop_variance.json now contains a measured normal-model probability for 10 of those 88 rows and describes the other 78 as unpriced for want of a measured input. Republished here as the exact split (10 priced / 78 unpriced) so the number is not read as 0 of 88 by a reader who never opens the variance page. This is the same request as R-26-1 on the board; it is restated because it is still true and because the decision it blocks (whether a prop is ever bettable) depends on it.

items.title: data/live/s14x/luck_skill.json uses a Pythagorean exponent that is not an NBA.com value
items.detail: The luck decomposition computes each team's expected wins from points for and against with exponent 13.91, the value Basketball-Reference publishes for the NBA. That is a published outside convention, not an NBA-operated figure, so the column is labelled everywhere it appears. The exponent's effect is small (a change to 14.0 moves no team's luck figure by more than a hundredth of a win on this sample) but the provenance is stated rather than implied.
items.affected: data/live/s14x/luck_skill.json, Luck page
items.suggested_action: If an NBA-operated source ever publishes an expected-win figure, replace this column with it and retire the outside convention.

items.title: The horizon's rest figures are lower bounds, because two official dates have no rows
items.detail: Rest is derived from official game DATES. The official log has no rows for 2026-10-24 and 2026-11-02, so a rest figure that spans either date is measured from the previous dated game and is therefore a LOWER bound on days off. This affects only the first days of the horizon; every 11/14-11/17 row whose last game is on or after 2026-11-06 is exact. Values that cannot be computed are left blank, never defaulted to 0.
items.affected: data/live/s14x/gameflow.json
items.suggested_action: Fill the two dates once readable, then rebuild the rest layer.
